name: Dunes
notes: Coastal and inland sand dunes: sand-binding rhizomatous grasses on mobile foredunes, sedges and creeping herbs behind, and scattered pine/juniper/willow scrub on stabilised grey dunes. Drawn on Atlantic and Baltic Europe, eastern and Pacific North America, and Australian foredunes.

canopy.name: Scots pine
canopy.source: Pinus sylvestris, Eurasia, planted and native on stabilised dunes (Baltic, Dutch coast), 15-35 m — Wikipedia

canopy.name: Dune pine
canopy.source: Pinus contorta subsp. contorta (shore pine), Pacific NW dunes Alaska-California, wind-stunted 5-15 m — Wikipedia / USDA

shrub.name: Creeping willow
shrub.source: Salix repens (incl. var. argentea), European dune slacks and grey dunes, low creeping willow 0.3-1.5 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Coastal juniper
shrub.source: Juniperus communis, circumboreal, common on stabilised European and North American dunes, prostrate to 4 m — Wikipedia

shrub.name: Bayberry
shrub.source: Morella pensylvanica, NE North American Atlantic dunes, aromatic thicket shrub 1-3 m — Wikipedia / USDA

shrub.name: Coastal wattle
shrub.source: Acacia longifolia subsp. sophorae, SE Australian dunes (invasive in S Africa/Portugal), sprawling 1.5-6 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Marram grass
ground.source: Ammophila arenaria, European Atlantic/Mediterranean foredunes (A. breviligulata in NE America), the archetypal sand-binder, 0.6-1.2 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: American beachgrass
ground.source: Ammophila breviligulata, Great Lakes and NE Atlantic dunes, rhizomatous foredune grass 0.6-1 m — USDA Plants

ground.name: Sea oats
ground.source: Uniola paniculata, SE US Atlantic/Gulf and Caribbean foredunes, tall nodding seed heads 1-2 m — Wikipedia / USDA

ground.name: Lyme grass
ground.source: Leymus arenarius, N European and Icelandic coastal dunes, blue-grey rhizomatous grass 0.6-1.5 m — Wikipedia

ground.name: Sand sedge
ground.source: Carex arenaria, European dunes, runs in straight lines from long rhizomes across bare sand, 10-40 cm — Wikipedia

ground.name: Dune evening primrose
ground.source: Oenothera drummondii, Gulf of Mexico dunes (widely naturalised), yellow-flowered sprawling herb 20-60 cm — Wikipedia

associations.name: Marram foredune
associations.where: mobile yellow dunes facing the sea, bare drifting sand
associations.source: Ammophila/Uniola mobile dune (Rodwell 2000 SD6; Ellenberg 1988 Ammophilion)

associations.name: Sand sedge grey dune
associations.where: stabilised inland dunes, thin humus over sand, dry
associations.source: Carex arenaria fixed dune grassland (Rodwell 2000 SD10/SD11; Koelerion)

associations.name: Creeping willow dune slack
associations.where: wet hollows between dunes reaching the water table
associations.source: Salix repens dune slack (Rodwell 2000 SD15/SD16; Ranwell 1972)

associations.name: Pine-juniper dune wood
associations.where: old stabilised dune ridges far from the sea, dry poor sand
associations.source: Dune pine wood and Juniperus scrub (Rodwell 2000 SD; Ellenberg 1988; EU habitat 2180)

associations.name: Coastal wattle dune scrub
associations.where: sheltered lee slopes and back dunes of Australian foredunes, sandy
associations.source: Acacia longifolia var. sophorae foredune scrub (Specht 1970; NSW coastal dune scrub)
